name: Origami tamper seal
subtitle: a seal that cannot be opened unnoticed

effects.effect: DNA strands fold themselves into any designed nanoscale shape
crystals a few nanometres wide glow in a colour set purely by their size

effect: DNA strands fold themselves into any designed nanoscale shape
how: A shipment of vaccines, a ballot box or a sealed instrument can be opened and closed again by anyone patient enough to copy the sticker. This seal is a film of folded DNA plates, each holding two coloured dots at a spacing set when the plate was folded, so the film glows a precise mixed colour that depends on a fold pattern nobody else knows. Breaking the seal unfolds the plates and the colour shifts; the pattern is too intricate to copy without the original design file.
obstacle: DNA films are delicate in heat and humidity, so the seal may change colour in a hot warehouse without anyone touching it.
why: Origami colour rulers work in the lab; field durability decides whether a seal is useful.
real: DNA-origami-placed plasmonic nanoparticle assemblies have been demonstrated as unclonable optical authentication labels (Dass/Liedl), and non-DNA optical PUF tamper-indicating seals exist, but no seal whose optical signature changes on opening via unfolding origami was found.
